## Discovery & Translational Science

* **Bacteriophage T7 kinase drives promiscuous host protein phosphorylation** [Science](https://www.science.org/content/blog-post/phosphorylate-and-spare-not)
  * Bacteriophage T7 kinase (T7K) was identified as an exceptionally promiscuous kinase that phosphorylates host proteins across *E. coli*, displaying specific affinity for DNA-binding domains.
  * Sticking negatively charged phosphate groups directly into DNA-binding sites disrupts target binding affinity and inhibits multiple host defense systems.

* **Childhood platinum chemotherapy linked to liver cellular aging** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/09/10/childhood-chemotherapy-cisplatin-carboplatin-new-study-liver-impact/)
  * Cisplatin and carboplatin treatments induce mutations in pediatric patients that accelerate the aging profile of liver cells to resemble adult cells.
  * Authors note these structural genomic changes may elevate the long-term risk of secondary liver tumors in cancer survivors.

* **Mathematical model explains attenuated semaglutide weight loss in type 2 diabetes** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.08.750112)
  * Human energy balance modeling shows that dynamic changes in urinary glucose excretion (UGE) and energy expenditure following improved glycemic control account for reduced weight loss in type 2 diabetes (T2D) patients compared to non-diabetic individuals.
  * Simulations suggest T2D patients receiving background SGLT2 inhibitor therapy experience the greatest attenuation of GLP-1-induced weight loss.

* **PKCδ deficiency reprograms macrophage immunometabolism to stabilize plaques** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42722701/)
  * Loss of protein kinase Cδ (PKCδ) reprograms macrophage immunometabolism, suppressing pyroptosis in atherosclerotic models.
  * The metabolic transition stabilizes atherosclerotic plaques, offering a prospective therapeutic target in cardiovascular disease.

* **Single-cell functional mapping prioritizes motor cortex PVALB⁺ neurons in MDD** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.08.26362568)
  * Integration of major depressive disorder (MDD) genome-wide association studies across >5 million single cells identified primary motor cortex (M1) PVALB⁺ inhibitory neurons as key drivers of genetic risk.
  * Integrated gene prioritization nominated *CNNM2* as a leading PVALB⁺-linked risk gene associated with synaptic and membrane-potential regulation.

* **Genetic analysis decouples osteoarthritis from Parkinson's disease** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.05.26362301)
  * Triangulation across cohort data, Mendelian randomization, and single-cell expression revealed no genetic correlation or causal link between osteoarthritis and Parkinson's disease, overturning prior observational hypotheses.
  * Observational associations appear largely driven by confounding factors such as depression-mediated attenuation.

## Early Trials — Phase I–II

* **[Big Pharma]** **Teclistamab demonstrates superior complete response in Phase 2 smoldering myeloma study** [Nature Medicine](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-026-04642-w)
  * The randomized Phase 2 ImmunoPRISM trial compared BCMA-targeting bispecific antibody teclistamab against lenalidomide-dexamethasone in high-risk smoldering multiple myeloma.
  * Patients treated with teclistamab achieved higher complete response rates, although extended follow-up is required to evaluate long-term prevention of progression to active multiple myeloma.

* **Phase 1 trial evaluates Online Proton Adaptive RadioTherapY** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42722207/)
  * A Phase 1 study initiated clinical evaluation of the PARTY (Online Proton Adaptive RadioTherapY) protocol.
  * The study assesses feasibility and technical workflow execution for adaptive daily proton radiation therapy dosing.

## Late & Pivotal Trials — Phase III

* **[Biotech]** **Oveporexton Phase 3 trials published for Narcolepsy Type 1** [NEJM](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2601598?af=R&rss=currentIssue)
  * Results from two Phase 3 trials evaluated the oral, selective orexin receptor 2 agonist oveporexton in patients with narcolepsy type 1.
  * Treatment provided targeted restoration of orexin pathway signaling, addressing the underlying hypocretin deficiency in affected patients.

* **Lifestyle therapy non-inferior to CBT in 358-patient mood disorder trial** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.08.26362466)
  * A randomized, single-blind trial in 358 adults with major depressive or bipolar disorder compared dietitian- and exercise physiologist-led lifestyle intervention to cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) via telehealth.
  * Lifestyle therapy met the prespecified non-inferiority margin (-1.6 points) for MADRS depressive symptom reduction at 8 weeks.

## Regulatory & Approvals

* **[Biotech]** **FDA places partial clinical hold on Biohaven’s Phase 3 epilepsy drug opakalim** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/biohaven-fda-hold-opakalim-epilepsy-drug-trial/830013/)
  * The FDA requested additional safety data regarding a drug metabolite identified in rodent studies, instructing Biohaven to pause recruitment in the Phase 3 RISE-2 trial.
  * Patient dosing continues for existing participants in RISE-2, and the fully enrolled Phase 3 RISE-3 trial remains unaffected with readouts expected later this year.

* **[Biotech]** **FDA extends review period for zanzalintinib NDA** [BioStocks via X](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2098375675509977480)
  * The FDA extended the review period for Exelixis's New Drug Application for zanzalintinib by three months.
  * The updated PDUFA target action date is March 3, 2027.

* **[Big Pharma]** **FDA expands approval for Bayer lung cancer indication** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/09/10/biotech-news-fda-expands-bayer-lung-cancer-drug-approval/)
  * The FDA granted an expanded label approval for Bayer's oncology drug in non-small cell lung cancer.

* **FDA clears AI algorithm for EKG heart attack detection** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/09/11/fda-new-ekg-heart-attack-detection-algo-queen-of-hearts/)
  * The FDA cleared an AI software tool (Queen of Hearts) designed to analyze standard EKGs for acute myocardial infarctions and subtle patterns indicating arterial blockages.

* **FDA issues final order removing PABA and trolamine salicylate from OTC sunscreen monograph** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/understanding-over-counter-medicines/questions-and-answers-fdas-regulatory-actions-over-counter-sunscreen)
  * A final administrative order removed aminobenzoic acid (PABA) and trolamine salicylate from the OTC sunscreen monograph after safety reviews concluded their risks outweigh benefits.
  * The action follows the agency's June 2026 decision to add bemotrizinol as an approved active ingredient.

## Business & Strategy

* **[Big Pharma]** **Cardiovascular pipeline setbacks spark investor pressure and strategic fallout** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/09/11/novartis-novo-nordisk-cardiovascular-drug-trials-fallout/)
  * Successive clinical trial failures of major cardiovascular drug candidates from Novartis and Novo Nordisk have raised industry concerns regarding target risk in late-stage cardiovascular development.
  * Following a sharp decline in share price, a major Novartis shareholder has publicly requested a board restructuring.

* **[Biotech]** **Biotech reverse mergers double in 2026 amid Wall Street shell demand** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/biotech-reverse-mergers-public-markets-ipo/829197/)
  * Roughly two dozen clinical-stage biotechs have announced reverse mergers into public shell companies so far in 2026, more than double the total seen across 2025.
  * Startups are increasingly leveraging reverse mergers to bypass traditional IPO bottlenecks and bring asset pipelines into public markets.

## Public Health & Policy

* **Mass gathering wastewater surveillance reveals stable viral dynamics at 2026 World Cup** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.04.26362178)
  * Analysis of 5,137 metagenomic wastewater samples collected across 17 Texas host and non-host cities during the 2026 FIFA World Cup showed no tournament-associated spike in respiratory or rare pathogens.
  * Findings support continuous baseline wastewater monitoring over event-triggered deployments.

* **Survey highlights operational stress among Bundibugyo Ebola virus outbreak workers** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.08.26362489)
  * A survey of field personnel responding to the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo documented widespread operational strain.
  * Sixty-one percent of respondents reported insufficient staffing, and 67% received one or zero rest days per week while working under active conflict conditions.

* **Administration proposes $500 ACA refunds ahead of elections** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/09/10/trump-affordable-care-act-refund-checks-who-is-eligible/)
  * A proposal was floated to offer $500 refund checks to select individuals enrolled in Affordable Care Act plans.
  * The legal mechanism and exact eligibility criteria governing the proposed disbursements remain unclarified.

**Worth watching:** Readout timing on Biohaven's fully enrolled RISE-3 trial following the FDA's partial hold on RISE-2, alongside industry movement on orexin receptor 2 agonists in sleep disorders.

youtube.markdown:
- Biology & Health
    - [Aging Genes can be Turned Off, if you do This Regularly](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cU5r6E-mwpg) -- Physionic
        - Physical exercise delays molecular aging and preserves energy metabolism in human skeletal muscle.
        - Training is associated with younger methylome and transcriptome profiles in skeletal muscle tissue.
        - Resistance exercise has been demonstrated to reverse age-related gene expression patterns in human skeletal muscle.
    - [Exercise for preserving cognitive function | Peter Attia, M.D.](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/1RYoai-ec_8) -- Peter Attia MD
        - Examines the relationship between lipids, cardiovascular disease, and Alzheimer's disease, including the potential impact of statins on neurodegenerative disorders.
        - Explores approaches for identifying impactful, practical strategies to improve healthspan and cognitive function.
        - Frames supplements as supportive tools rather than primary solutions within longevity and health optimization strategies.
- Pure Science
    - [The Scariest Chart In Engineering](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/O3a99HNskNk) -- Veritasium
        - Focuses on the Smith Chart, a visual calculation tool used in RF and microwave electrical engineering.
        - Demonstrates how the chart works mathematically and conceptually to solve transmission line and impedance matching problems.
        - Uses a record-sized physical printout of the Smith Chart to break down its complex polar grid layout for viewers.
- Other
    - [How Do Fossils Form?: Crash Course Geology #18](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iWUp2kMCv6o) -- CrashCourse
        - Covers the biological and geological processes required for organisms to become fossilized, using examples like the Nodosaur.
        - Explains the environmental and physical factors that make fossilization an extremely rare occurrence.
        - Details what fossils reveal about ancient environments, evolutionary timelines, and Earth's geological history.
- To watch
    - [The most significant moment in modern robotics.](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/7BbL2leRv3w) -- Welch Labs
